Voice typing now hands you written text instead of a transcript. Until now what landed at your cursor was exactly what the speech recogniser heard: the "呃" and the "然後", the false start you talked over, the sentence that ran for half a minute without a comma in it. Everything you said, and none of the shape you would have given it had you typed it.

The transcript now goes past a model on its way to the clipboard. Filler words and false starts come out, punctuation goes in, and paragraphs land where a writer would put them. Your wording stays yours — this is a tidy-up, not a rewrite. It will not answer a question you happened to dictate, and it will not summarise you.

It runs in the one place it can: between the transcript settling and the paste. Voice typing puts text into whatever app you were in by simulating ⌘V, and that keystroke is one-way — so the moment before it is the last moment the text is still Parley's to change. That makes the clean-up something you wait for, which is why it is built so the wait is short and never wasted.

Two seconds, and then your raw words go out regardless. Losing a tidy-up costs a few filler words; waiting costs you your train of thought. Short phrases skip the round trip entirely, because an eight-character reply has no filler to remove and is exactly where a pause is felt. And if what comes back is not a clean-up — an answer, a summary, a translation, a truncation, or Traditional Chinese quietly turned into Simplified — it is discarded and you get your own words instead.

Words in your personal dictionary travel with the request as terms to leave alone. Those are words you already corrected by hand once; having them "fixed" back would be worse than no polish at all.

The model comes from your realtime lane, so whatever is configured there does the work: a local Ollama model keeps the transcript on your machine, and a hosted key sends it wherever that key already sends your meeting analysis. Nothing new goes anywhere. If that lane has no provider configured, the setting says so rather than quietly doing nothing.

On by default, under Settings → Voice typing.
